Answer: C
Reason: The image shows a thin-walled cavitary lesion in the right mid-zone, and when combined with the clinical presentation of acute chest pain and mild fever, this is most characteristic of a cavitating pulmonary infarction (often secondary to pulmonary embolism). Other options like tuberculosis or abscess typically present with thick-walled cavities and a more subacute or severe infectious course, while malignancy usually has thicker, irregular walls.
